637: static void handle_ack(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message)
638: {

640:   struct active_transaction *active;
641:   bool replay;
642:   int result;
643:   uint32_t reason;
644:

647:   if (active == NULL)

653:   g_stats.last_active_header = active->message.header;

657:       g_stats.bad_ack++;
658:       g_stats.bad_ack_reason |= reason;
659:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, g_stats.last_ack_header);
660:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, g_stats.last_active_header);
661:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, g_stats.bad_ack_reason);
662:       return;
663:     }
664: 
665: 
666:   if (bk7258_mb_header_channel(message) == BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX &&

671:       g_stats.bad_ack++;

674:       return;
675:     }
676: 
677:   if ((bk7258_mb_header_state(message) & ~BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL) != 0)
678:     {
679:       g_stats.bad_ack++;
680:       g_stats.bad_ack_reason |= 64u;
681:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, g_stats.bad_ack_reason);
682:       return;
683:     }
684: 
685:   result = (bk7258_mb_header_state(message) & BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL) != 0 ?
686:            -EREMOTEIO : OK;
687: 
688:   if (bk7258_mb_header_channel(message) == BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX &&
689:       result == OK && (message->payload_address & 2u) != 0)
690:     {
691:       result = -EREMOTEIO;
692:     }
693: 
694:   replay = active == &epoch->probe && epoch->replay;
695:   release_acks_before(replay ? epoch->first_probe_order : active->order);

698:       unsigned int replay_index = g_recovery_index;
699:       unsigned int i;
700: 
701:       /* This ACK may be a late ACK for the original copy.  It proves every
702:        * older epoch was copied, but not that the new replay envelope was

715:         }
716: 
717:       select_recovery_epoch();
718:       (void)dispatch_locked();
719:       return;
720:     }
721: 
722:   complete_transaction(active, message, result);
723: 
724:   if (active == &epoch->probe)
725:     {
726:       if (result == OK && (message->flags & 2u) == 0)
727:         {
728:           release_recovery_slots();
729:           g_recovery_index = 0;
730:           g_probe_attempts = 0;
731:           set_link_state(BK7258_MB_LINK_READY);

1428:       queued = g_channels[index].queued;

1430:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);

163: static bool valid_ack(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack)
164: {
165:   return ack != NULL && (ack->payload_address & ~3u) == 0 &&
166:          ack->payload_length == 0 && ack->flags == 0 && ack->crc8 == 0 &&
167:          ack->reserved == 0;
168: }
169: 
170: static void mb_uart_tx_complete(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack,
171:                                 int result, void *arg)
172: {
173:   uint8_t command;
174:   bool failed;
175: 
176:   (void)arg;
177:   /* The mailbox transport invokes completion callbacks while holding
178:    * g_bk7258_driver_lock.  Do not reacquire the non-recursive SMP lock here.
179:    */
180:   command = ack == NULL ? g_uart.transaction_command :
181:             bk7258_mb_header_cmd(ack);
182:   failed = result < 0 || !valid_ack(ack) ||
183:            (ack != NULL && (ack->payload_address & 2u) != 0);
184: 
185:   if (ack != NULL && valid_ack(ack))
186:     {
187:       g_uart.peer_rts = (ack->payload_address & 1u) != 0;
188:       g_uart.peer_rts_known = true;
189:     }
190: 
191:   if (result == -ETIMEDOUT || result == -ECONNRESET)
192:     {
193:       g_uart.peer_rts_known = false;
194:       g_uart.state_pending = true;
195:     }
196: 
197:   if (command == BK7258_MB_UART_DATA && g_uart.tx_inflight != 0)
198:     {
199:       if (!failed)
200:         {
201:           g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
202:                            MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
203:           g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
204:         }
205:       else if (result == -ETIMEDOUT || result == -ECONNRESET)
206:         {
207:           /* A failed/unknown ACK cannot tell whether CP consumed the bytes.
208:            * Drop this local chunk rather than replaying terminal characters.
209:            */
210: 
211:           g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
212:                            MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
213:           g_uart.stats.tx_unknown++;
214:           g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
215:           g_uart.stats.resets++;
216:         }
217:       else
218:         {
219:           g_uart.stats.remote_fail++;
220:           g_uart.state_pending = true;
221:           if (g_uart.tx_retry_count == 0)
222:             {
223:               /* Keep tx_read unchanged.  The same chunk may be copied again
224:                * once STATE recovery succeeds, but only once.
225:                */
226: 
227:               g_uart.tx_retry_count = 1;
228:               g_uart.stats.tx_retry++;
229:             }
230:           else
231:             {
232:               g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
233:                                MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
234:               g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
235:               g_uart.stats.tx_retry_drop++;
236:             }
237:         }
238: 
239:       g_uart.tx_inflight = 0;
240:     }
241:   else if (command == BK7258_MB_UART_STATE && failed)
242:     {
243:       g_uart.stats.remote_fail++;
244:       /* The transport invokes this completion before it changes READY to
245:        * ABORTING.  Always retain a STATE request so RESET recovery has a
246:        * probe to send after it reaches PROBING.
247:        */
248: 
249:       g_uart.state_pending = true;
250:     }
251: 
252:   g_uart.transaction_busy = false;
253:   nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
254: }
255: 
256: static int mb_uart_receive(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message,
257:                            uint8_t *ack_flags, void *arg)
258: {
259:   uint8_t command = bk7258_mb_header_cmd(message);
260:   uint16_t length = message->payload_length;
261:   uint16_t first;
262:   bool failed = false;
263:   bool malformed = false;
264: 
265:   (void)arg;
266:   if (ack_flags == NULL)
267:     {
268:       return -EINVAL;
269:     }
270: 
271:   if (command != BK7258_MB_UART_DATA && command != BK7258_MB_UART_STATE)
272:     {
273:       g_uart.stats.bad_flags++;
274:       failed = true;
275:       malformed = true;
276:     }
277:   else if ((message->flags & ~1u) != 0)
278:     {
279:       g_uart.stats.bad_flags++;
280:       failed = true;
281:       malformed = true;
282:     }
283:   else if (message->crc8 != 0)
284:     {
285:       g_uart.stats.bad_crc++;
286:       g_uart.sticky_status |= MB_UART_STATUS_PARITY;
287:       failed = true;
288:       malformed = true;
289:     }
290:   else if (message->reserved != 0)
291:     {
292:       g_uart.stats.bad_reserved++;
293:       failed = true;
294:       malformed = true;
295:     }
296: 
297:   if (!failed && command == BK7258_MB_UART_DATA)
298:     {
299:       if (message->payload_address != BK7258_MB_UART_RX_ADDRESS)
300:         {
301:           g_uart.stats.bad_pointer++;
302:           failed = true;
303:           malformed = true;
304:         }
305:       else if (length == 0 || length > BK7258_MB_UART_CHUNK_SIZE)
306:         {
307:           g_uart.stats.bad_length++;
308:           failed = true;
309:           malformed = true;
310:         }
311:       else if (!bk7258_mailbox_link_ready())
312:         {
313:           failed = true;
314:         }
315:       else if (rx_free() < length)
316:         {
317:           g_uart.stats.rx_overflow++;
318:           g_uart.sticky_status |= MB_UART_STATUS_OVF;
319:           failed = true;
320:         }
321:       else
322:         {
323:           const uint8_t *source =
324:             (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)BK7258_MB_UART_RX_ADDRESS;
325: 
326:           __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
327:           first = MB_UART_RX_SIZE - g_uart.rx_write;
328:           if (first > length)
329:             {
330:               first = length;
331:             }
332: 
333:           memcpy(&g_uart.rx_ring[g_uart.rx_write], source, first);
334:           if (first != length)
335:             {
336:               memcpy(g_uart.rx_ring, source + first, length - first);
337:             }
338: 
339:           g_uart.rx_write = (g_uart.rx_write + length) % MB_UART_RX_SIZE;
340:           g_uart.stats.data_rx++;
341:           g_uart.stats.rx_bytes += length;
342:         }
343:     }
344:   else if (!failed)
345:     {
346:       if (message->payload_address != 0 || message->payload_length != 0)
347:         {
348:           g_uart.stats.bad_length++;
349:           failed = true;
350:           malformed = true;
351:         }
352:       else
353:         {
354:           g_uart.stats.state_rx++;
355:         }
356:     }
357: 
358:   if (!malformed)
359:     {
360:       bool old_peer_rts = g_uart.peer_rts;
361: 
362:       g_uart.peer_rts = (message->flags & 1u) != 0;
363:       g_uart.peer_rts_known = true;
364:       if (old_peer_rts && !g_uart.peer_rts)
365:         {
366:           nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
367:         }
368:     }
369: 
370:   update_local_rts();
371:   *ack_flags = (g_uart.local_rts ? 1u : 0u) | (failed ? 2u : 0u);
372:   nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
373:   return malformed ? -EPROTO : OK;
374: }

376: static int send_state_locked(void)
377: {
378:   struct bk7258_mb_wire_message message;
379:   int ret;
380: 
381:   memset(&message, 0, sizeof(message));
382:   message.header = bk7258_mb_make_header(BK7258_MB_UART_STATE, 0, 0, 0,
383:                                          BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX);
384:   message.flags = g_uart.local_rts ? 1u : 0u;
385:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX, &message,
386:                                   mb_uart_tx_complete, NULL);
387:   if (ret == OK)
388:     {
389:       g_uart.transaction_busy = true;
390:       g_uart.transaction_command = BK7258_MB_UART_STATE;
391:       g_uart.state_pending = false;
392:       g_uart.stats.state_tx++;
393:     }
394: 
395:   return ret;
396: }
397: 
398: static int send_data_locked(void)
399: {
400:   struct bk7258_mb_wire_message message;
401:   uint8_t *destination =
402:     (uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)BK7258_MB_UART_TX_ADDRESS;
403:   uint16_t length = tx_count();
404:   uint16_t first;
405:   int ret;
406: 
407:   if (length > BK7258_MB_UART_CHUNK_SIZE)
408:     {
409:       length = BK7258_MB_UART_CHUNK_SIZE;
410:     }
411: 
412:   if (length == 0 || g_uart.peer_rts)
413:     {
414:       return -EAGAIN;
415:     }
416: 
417:   first = MB_UART_TX_SIZE - g_uart.tx_read;
418:   if (first > length)
419:     {
420:       first = length;
421:     }
422: 
423:   memcpy(destination, &g_uart.tx_ring[g_uart.tx_read], first);
424:   if (first != length)
425:     {
426:       memcpy(destination + first, g_uart.tx_ring, length - first);
427:     }
428: 
429:   memset(&message, 0, sizeof(message));
430:   message.header = bk7258_mb_make_header(BK7258_MB_UART_DATA, 0, 0, 0,
431:                                          BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX);
432:   message.payload_address = BK7258_MB_UART_TX_ADDRESS;
433:   message.payload_length = length;
434:   message.flags = g_uart.local_rts ? 1u : 0u;
435:   __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
436:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX, &message,
437:                                   mb_uart_tx_complete, NULL);
438:   if (ret == OK)
439:     {
440:       g_uart.transaction_busy = true;
441:       g_uart.transaction_command = BK7258_MB_UART_DATA;
442:       g_uart.tx_inflight = length;
443:       g_uart.stats.data_tx++;
444:     }
445: 
446:   return ret;
447: }

449: static int mb_uart_worker(int argc, char **argv)
450: {
451:   int ret;
452: 
453:   (void)argc;
454:   (void)argv;
455:   ret = bind_worker_to_primary();
456:   if (ret < 0)
457:     {
458:       return -EXDEV;
459:     }
460: 
461:   for (;;)
462:     {
463:       bk7258_mb_uart_callback_t callback;
464:       void *callback_arg;
465:       irqstate_t flags;
466: 
467:       (void)nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&g_uart.worker_sem,
468:                                            MB_UART_WORK_INTERVAL);
469:       nxsem_reset(&g_uart.worker_sem, 0);
470:       flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
471: 
472:       if (!g_uart.transaction_busy)
473:         {
474:           enum bk7258_mb_link_state link = bk7258_mailbox_link_state();
475: 
476:           if (link == BK7258_MB_LINK_PROBING && g_uart.state_pending)
477:             {
478:               (void)send_state_locked();
479:             }
480:           else if (link == BK7258_MB_LINK_READY)
481:             {
482:               if (g_uart.state_pending)
483:                 {
484:                   (void)send_state_locked();
485:                 }
486:               else
487:                 {
488:                   (void)send_data_locked();
489:                 }
490:             }
491:         }
492: 
493:       callback = g_uart.callback;
494:       callback_arg = g_uart.callback_arg;
495:       rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
496: 
497:       if (callback != NULL)
498:         {
499:           callback(callback_arg);
500:         }
501:     }
502: 
503:   return OK;
504: }

506: void bk7258_mbox_uart_early_init(void)
507: {
508:   /* The zero-initialized TX ring accepts bounded early logs before MBOX0 is
509:    * available.  Full rings return an accurate short write.
510:    */
511: }

513: int bk7258_mb_uart_init(void)
514: {
515:   int ret;
516: 
517:   if (g_uart.initialized)
518:     {
519:       return OK;
520:     }
521: 
522:   /* Keep early TX data and its indices. */
523: 
524:   g_uart.rx_read = 0;
525:   g_uart.rx_write = 0;
526:   g_uart.tx_inflight = 0;
527:   g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
528:   g_uart.sticky_status = 0;
529:   g_uart.transaction_busy = false;
530:   g_uart.transaction_command = BK7258_MB_UART_STATE;
531:   g_uart.state_pending = true;
532:   g_uart.local_rts = false;
533:   g_uart.upper_rts = false;
534:   g_uart.peer_rts = false;
535:   g_uart.peer_rts_known = false;
536:   memset(&g_uart.stats, 0, sizeof(g_uart.stats));
537:   nxsem_init(&g_uart.worker_sem, 0, 0);
538:   g_worker_created = false;
539:   g_worker_pid = -1;
540: 
541:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_register_rx(BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_RX,
542:                                     mb_uart_receive, NULL);
543:   if (ret < 0)
544:     {
545:       return ret;
546:     }
547:   g_uart.initialized = true;
548:   return OK;
549: }

551: int bk7258_mb_uart_worker_start(void)
552: {
553:   int ret;
554: 
555:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_UART_WORKER_ENTER);
556: 
557:   if (!g_uart.initialized)
558:     {
559:       return -EAGAIN;
560:     }
561: 
562:   if (!g_worker_created)
563:     {
564:       bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_UART_CREATE_ENTER);
565:       /* Early console writes may have posted before this worker existed.
566:        * Collapse those stale wakeups; the TX ring and state_pending retain
567:        * all work that must actually be processed. */
568: 
569:       nxsem_reset(&g_uart.worker_sem, 0);
570:       ret = kthread_create("mb-uart0", MB_UART_PRIORITY, 2048,
571:                            mb_uart_worker, NULL);
572:       if (ret < 0)
573:         {
574:           return ret;
575:         }
576: 
577:       bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_UART_CREATE_RETURN);
578:       g_worker_created = true;
579:       g_worker_pid = ret;
580:     }
581: 
582:   return OK;
583: }

585: int bk7258_mb_uart_worker_activate(void)
586: {
587:   struct sched_param param;
588: 
589:   if (!g_worker_created || g_worker_pid < 0)
590:     {
591:       return -EAGAIN;
592:     }
593: 
594:   param.sched_priority = MB_UART_PRIORITY;
595:   return sched_setparam(g_worker_pid, &param) < 0 ? -errno : OK;
596: }

628: ssize_t bk7258_mbox_uart_write(const uint8_t *data, size_t length)
629: {
630:   irqstate_t flags;
631:   uint16_t available;
632:   uint16_t written;
633:   uint16_t first;
634: 
635:   if (data == NULL && length != 0)
636:     {
637:       return -EINVAL;
638:     }
639: 
640:   if (length == 0)
641:     {
642:       return 0;
643:     }
644: 
645:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
646:   available = tx_free();
647:   written = length > available ? available : length;
648:   first = MB_UART_TX_SIZE - g_uart.tx_write;
649:   if (first > written)
650:     {
651:       first = written;
652:     }
653: 
654:   memcpy(&g_uart.tx_ring[g_uart.tx_write], data, first);
655:   if (first != written)
656:     {
657:       memcpy(g_uart.tx_ring, data + first, written - first);
658:     }
659: 
660:   g_uart.tx_write = (g_uart.tx_write + written) % MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
661:   g_uart.stats.write_calls++;
662:   g_uart.stats.write_bytes += written;
663:   if (written < length)
664:     {
665:       g_uart.stats.short_writes++;
666:     }
667: 
668:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
669:   if (g_uart.initialized && written != 0)
670:     {
671:       nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
672:     }
673: 
674:   return written;
675: }

677: ssize_t bk7258_mbox_uart_read(uint8_t *data, size_t length,
678:                               unsigned int *status)
679: {
680:   irqstate_t flags;
681:   uint16_t available;
682:   uint16_t count;
683:   uint16_t first;
684: 
685:   if (data == NULL || length == 0)
686:     {
687:       return -EINVAL;
688:     }
689: 
690:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
691:   available = rx_count();
692:   count = length > available ? available : length;
693:   first = MB_UART_RX_SIZE - g_uart.rx_read;
694:   if (first > count)
695:     {
696:       first = count;
697:     }
698: 
699:   memcpy(data, &g_uart.rx_ring[g_uart.rx_read], first);
700:   if (first != count)
701:     {
702:       memcpy(data + first, g_uart.rx_ring, count - first);
703:     }
704: 
705:   g_uart.rx_read = (g_uart.rx_read + count) % MB_UART_RX_SIZE;
706:   if (status != NULL)
707:     {
708:       *status = g_uart.sticky_status;
709:       g_uart.sticky_status = 0;
710:     }
711: 
712:   if (!g_uart.upper_rts && g_uart.local_rts &&
713:       rx_count() < MB_UART_RTS_RELEASE)
714:     {
715:       update_local_rts();
716:     }
717: 
718:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
719:   if (g_uart.initialized && count != 0)
720:     {
721:       nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
722:     }
723: 
724:   return count;
725: }

776: int bk7258_mbox_uart_flush(unsigned int timeout_ms)
777: {
778:   clock_t deadline = clock_systime_ticks() + MSEC2TICK(timeout_ms);
779: 
780:   if (!g_uart.initialized || !bk7258_mailbox_link_ready())
781:     {
782:       return -EAGAIN;
783:     }
784: 
785:   while (!bk7258_mbox_uart_txempty())
786:     {
787:       if ((int32_t)(clock_systime_ticks() - deadline) >= 0)
788:         {
789:           return -ETIMEDOUT;
790:         }
791: 
792:       nxsig_usleep(1000);
793:     }
794: 
795:   return OK;
796: }

798: void bk7258_mbox_uart_dump_stats(void)
799: {
800:   irqstate_t flags;
801:   struct mb_uart_stats stats;
802:   uint16_t tx;
803:   uint16_t rx;
804:   bool local_rts;
805:   bool peer_rts;
806: 
807:   flags = rspin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_driver_lock);
808:   stats = g_uart.stats;
809:   tx = tx_count();
810:   rx = rx_count();
811:   local_rts = g_uart.local_rts;
812:   peer_rts = g_uart.peer_rts;
813:   rspin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_driver_lock, flags);
814: 
815:   printf("mb-uart0: txq=%u rxq=%u rts=%u cts=%u data=%lu/%lu "
816:          "state=%lu/%lu short=%lu overflow=%lu bad=%lu/%lu/%lu/%lu/%lu "
817:          "remote=%lu retry=%lu/%lu unknown=%lu reset=%lu\n",
818:          tx, rx, local_rts, peer_rts,
819:          (unsigned long)stats.data_tx, (unsigned long)stats.data_rx,

23: 
24: #define BK7258_SYSTICK_RELOAD \
25:   ((CONFIG_BK7258_CPU_FREQ_HZ / TICK_PER_SEC) - 1u)
26: 
27: #if CONFIG_BK7258_CPU_FREQ_HZ % TICK_PER_SEC != 0
28: #  error "BK7258 CPU frequency must divide evenly into the system tick rate"
29: #endif
30: 
31: #if BK7258_SYSTICK_RELOAD > NVIC_MAX_SYSTICK_CNT
32: #  error "BK7258 SysTick reload exceeds the 24-bit counter"
33: #endif
34: 
35: static bool g_first_tick_complete;
36: static uint32_t g_tick_count;
37: 
38: static int bk7258_timerisr(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
39: {
40:   uint32_t tick = ++g_tick_count;
41:   bool first_tick = !g_first_tick_complete;
42: 
43:   (void)irq;
44:   (void)context;
45:   (void)arg;
46: 
47:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(3, (tick << 8) | 1u);
48: 
49:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(3, (tick << 8) | 2u);
50:   nxsched_process_timer();
51:   bk7258_boottrace_detail(3, (tick << 8) | 3u);
52: 
53:   if (first_tick)
54:     {
55:       g_first_tick_complete = true;
56:     }
57: 
58:   return OK;
59: }
60: 
61: int bk7258_timer_start(void)
62: {
63:   if (up_cpu_index() != 0)
64:     {
65:       return -EXDEV;
66:     }
67: 
68:   putreg32(0, NVIC_SYSTICK_CURRENT);
69:   bk7258_boottrace_primary(BK7258_BOOT_SYSTICK_STARTED);
70:   putreg32(NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_CLKSOURCE | NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_TICKINT |
71:            NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL_ENABLE, NVIC_SYSTICK_CTRL);
72:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_SYSTICK);
73:   return OK;
74: }

76: void up_timer_initialize(void)
77: {
78:   uint32_t priority;
79: 
80:   /* Match the vendor SMP port's configTICK_CORE contract: only logical CPU0
81:    * owns the global tick.  CPU1 leaves its private SysTick disabled.
82:    */
83: 
84:   DEBUGASSERT(up_cpu_index() == 0);

204: static void mbox_process_desc(void)

206:   struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
207:   int ret;
208: 
209:   /* ACK and RESET never need ACK slots.  Process them ahead of a deferred
210:    * ordinary command, then retry ordinary commands in original FIFO order.
211:    */
212: 
213:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(true)) != NULL)
214:     {
215:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
216:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
217:       g_processing_order = 0;
218:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)
219:         {
220:           g_stats.descriptor_deferred++;
221:           break;
222:         }
223: 
224:       desc->used = false;
225:     }
226: 
227:   while ((desc = mbox_oldest_desc(false)) != NULL)
228:     {
229:       g_processing_order = desc->order;
230:       ret = g_callback == NULL ? -ENOSYS : g_callback(&desc->message);
231:       g_processing_order = 0;
232:       if (ret == -EAGAIN)

234:           break;
235:         }

241: static int bk7258_mbox_irq(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
242: {
243:   uintptr_t rdata0;
244:   uintptr_t rdata1;
245:   uintptr_t sidreg;
246:   int cpu = up_cpu_index();
247:   unsigned int budget = MBOX_IRQ_DRAIN_BUDGET;
248: 
249:   (void)irq;
250:   (void)context;
251:   (void)arg;
252: 
253:   mbox_clear_errors(cpu);
254:   if (cpu == 1 && bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() >=
255:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_ACK &&
256:                   bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() <
257:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_ENTER)
258:     {
259:       bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_ENTER);
260:     }
261:   sidreg = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_SID : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_SID;
262:   rdata0 = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_RDATA0 : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_RDATA0;
263:   rdata1 = cpu == 0 ? BK7258_MBOX_CH1_RDATA1 : BK7258_MBOX_CH2_RDATA1;
264: 
265:   while ((bk7258_mbox_rx_status() & 2u) == 0 && budget-- != 0)
266:     {
267:       struct mbox_rx_descriptor *desc;
268:       uint32_t address;
269:       uint32_t length;
270:       uint8_t source;
271: 
272:       if (cpu == 0)
273:         {
274:           mbox_process_desc();
275:         }
276: 
277:       desc = cpu == 0 ? mbox_alloc_desc() : NULL;
278:       if (cpu == 0 && desc == NULL)
279:         {
280:           g_stats.descriptor_full++;
281:           mbox_trace_errors();
282:           break;
283:         }
284: 
285:       source = getreg32(sidreg) & 0x0fu;
286:       address = getreg32(rdata0);
287:       length = getreg32(rdata1);
288: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
289:       if (length == 0)
290:         {
291:           if (source == (uint8_t)(2 - cpu))
292:             {
293:               if (cpu == 1 && address == BK7258_MBOX_RAW_KICK)
294:                 {
295:                   bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_RAW);
296:                 }
297: 
298:               bk7258_smp_ipi_receive(irq, context, address);
299:             }
300:           else
301:             {
302:               if (cpu == 0)
303:                 {
304:                   g_stats.bad_source++;
305:                   mbox_trace_errors();
306:                 }
307:             }
308: 
309:           continue;
310:         }
311: #endif
312: 
313:       if (cpu != 0)
314:         {
315:           continue;
316:         }
317: 
318:       if (!mbox_valid_envelope(source, address, length))
319:         {
320:           continue;
321:         }
322: 
323:       __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
324:       memcpy(&desc->message, (const void *)(uintptr_t)address,
325:              sizeof(desc->message));
326:       desc->order = ++g_rx_order;
327:       desc->used = true;
328:       g_stats.rx_messages++;
329:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(0, desc->message.header);
330:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(1, address);
331:       bk7258_boottrace_detail(2, g_stats.rx_messages);
332:       mbox_process_desc();
333:     }
334: 
335:   if (cpu == 0)
336:     {
337:       mbox_process_desc();
338:     }
339: 
340:   if (cpu == 1 && bk7258_boottrace_secondary_stage() ==
341:                   BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_RAW)
342:     {
343:       bk7258_boottrace_secondary(BK7258_BOOT_SECONDARY_MBOX_EXIT);
344:     }
345: 
346:   return OK;
347: }

108: /****************************************************************************
109:  * Name: nxsem_reset
110:  *
111:  * Description:
112:  *   Reset a semaphore count to a specific value.  This is similar to part
113:  *   of the operation of nxsem_init().  But nxsem_reset() may need to wake up
114:  *   tasks waiting on a count.  This kind of operation is sometimes required
115:  *   within the OS (only) for certain error handling conditions.
116:  *
117:  *   Mutex is simply posted until it is not blocking any tasks. If the
118:  *   requested count is 0, a single running holder is left. If the requested
119:  *   count is 1, the mutex is set to "reset". Other requested counts are not
120:  *   allowed for mutex.
121:  *
122:  * Input Parameters:
123:  *   sem   - Semaphore descriptor to be reset
124:  *   count - The requested semaphore count
125:  *
126:  * Returned Value:
127:  *   This is an internal OS interface, not available to applications, and
128:  *   hence follows the NuttX internal error return policy:  Zero (OK) is
129:  *   returned on success.  A negated errno value is returned on failure.
130:  *
131:  ****************************************************************************/
132: 
133: int nxsem_reset(FAR sem_t *sem, int16_t count)
134: {
135:   irqstate_t flags;
136: 
137:   DEBUGASSERT(sem != NULL && count >= 0);
138: 
139:   /* Don't allow any context switches that may result from the following
140:    * nxsem_post() operations.
141:    */
142: 
143:   sched_lock();
144: 
145:   /* Prevent any access to the semaphore by interrupt handlers while we are
146:    * performing this operation.
147:    */
148: 
149:   flags = enter_critical_section();
150: 
151:   if (NXSEM_IS_MUTEX(sem))
152:     {
153:       reset_mutex(sem, count);
154:     }
155:   else
156:     {
157:       reset_sem(sem, count);
158:     }
159: 
160:   /* Allow any pending context switches to occur now */
161: 
162:   leave_critical_section(flags);
163:   sched_unlock();
164:   return OK;
165: }

42: /****************************************************************************
43:  * Name: nxsched_set_affinity
44:  *
45:  * Description:
46:  *   sched_setaffinity() sets the CPU affinity mask of the thread whose ID
47:  *   is pid to the value specified by mask.  If pid is zero, then the
48:  *   calling thread is used.  The argument cpusetsize is the length (i
49:  *   bytes) of the data pointed to by mask.  Normally this argument would
50:  *   be specified as sizeof(cpu_set_t).
51:  *
52:  *   If the thread specified by pid is not currently running on one of the
53:  *   CPUs specified in mask, then that thread is migrated to one of the
54:  *   CPUs specified in mask.
55:  *
56:  *   nxsched_set_affinity() is identical to the function sched_setparam(),
57:  *   differing only in its return value:  This function does not modify
58:  *   the errno variable.  This is a non-standard, internal OS function and
59:  *   is not intended for use by application logic.  Applications should
60:  *   use the standard sched_setparam().
61:  *
62:  * Input Parameters:
63:  *   pid        - The ID of thread whose affinity set will be modified.
64:  *   cpusetsize - Size of mask.  MUST be sizeofcpu_set_t().
65:  *   mask       - The location to return the thread's new affinity set.
66:  *
67:  * Returned Value:
68:  *   Zero (OK) if successful.  Otherwise, a negated errno value is returned:
69:  *
70:  *     ESRCH  The task whose ID is pid could not be found.
71:  *
72:  ****************************************************************************/
73: 
74: int nxsched_set_affinity(pid_t pid, size_t cpusetsize,
75:                          FAR const cpu_set_t *mask)
76: {
77:   FAR struct tcb_s *tcb;
78:   irqstate_t flags;
79:   int ret = OK;
80: 
81:   DEBUGASSERT(cpusetsize == sizeof(cpu_set_t) && mask != NULL);
82: 
83:   /* Make sure that affinity mask is valid */
84: 
85:   if (*mask == 0)
86:     {
87:       return -EINVAL;
88:     }
89: 
90:   /* Verify that the PID corresponds to a real task */
91: 
92:   if (!pid)
93:     {
94:       tcb = this_task();
95:     }
96:   else
97:     {
98:       tcb = nxsched_get_tcb(pid);
99:     }
100: 
101:   if (tcb == NULL)
102:     {
103:       ret = -ESRCH;
104:       goto errout;
105:     }
106: 
107:   /* Don't permit changing the affinity mask of any task locked to a CPU
108:    * (i.e., an IDLE task)
109:    */
110: 
111:   flags = enter_critical_section();
112:   if ((atomic_read(&tcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED) != 0)
113:     {
114:       ret = -EINVAL;
115:       goto errout_with_csection;
116:     }
117: 
118:   /* Set the new affinity mask. */
119: 
120:   tcb->affinity = *mask;
121: 
122:   /* Is the task still executing a a CPU in its affinity mask? Will this
123:    * change cause the task to be removed from its current assigned task
124:    * list?
125:    *
126:    * First... is the task in an assigned task list?
127:    */
128: 
129:   if (tcb->task_state >= FIRST_READY_TO_RUN_STATE &&
130:       tcb->task_state <= LAST_READY_TO_RUN_STATE)
131:     {
132:       /* Yes... is the CPU associated with the assigned task in the new
133:        * affinity mask?
134:        */
135: 
136:       if ((tcb->affinity & (1 << tcb->cpu)) == 0)
137:         {
138:           /* No.. then we will need to move the task from the assigned
139:            * task list to some other ready to run list.
140:            *
141:            * nxsched_set_priority() will do just what we want... it will
142:            * remove the task from its current position in the some assigned
143:            * task list and then simply put it back in the right place.  This
144:            * works even if the task is this task.
145:            */
146: 
147:           ret = nxsched_set_priority(tcb, tcb->sched_priority);
148:         }
149:     }
150: 
151: errout_with_csection:
152:   leave_critical_section(flags);
153:   if (pid)
154:     {
155:       nxsched_put_tcb(tcb);
156:     }
157: 
158: errout:
159:   return ret;
160: }

163:  * Name: sched_setaffinity
164:  *
165:  * Description:
166:  *   sched_setaffinity() sets the CPU affinity mask of the thread whose ID
167:  *   is pid to the value specified by mask.  If pid is zero, then the
168:  *   calling thread is used.  The argument cpusetsize is the length (i
169:  *   bytes) of the data pointed to by mask.  Normally this argument would
170:  *   be specified as sizeof(cpu_set_t).
171:  *
172:  *   If the thread specified by pid is not currently running on one of the
173:  *   CPUs specified in mask, then that thread is migrated to one of the
174:  *   CPUs specified in mask.
175:  *
176:  *   This function is a simply wrapper around nxsched_set_affinity() that
177:  *   sets the errno value in the event of an error.
178:  *
179:  * Input Parameters:
180:  *   pid        - The ID of thread whose affinity set will be modified.
181:  *   cpusetsize - Size of mask.  MUST be sizeofcpu_set_t().
182:  *   mask       - The location to return the thread's new affinity set.
183:  *
184:  * Returned Value:
185:  *   0 if successful.  Otherwise, ERROR (-1) is returned, and errno is
186:  *   set appropriately:
187:  *
188:  *     ESRCH  The task whose ID is pid could not be found.
189:  *
190:  ****************************************************************************/
191: 
192: int sched_setaffinity(pid_t pid, size_t cpusetsize,
193:                       FAR const cpu_set_t *mask)
194: {
195:   int ret = nxsched_set_affinity(pid, cpusetsize, mask);
196:   if (ret < 0)
197:     {
198:       set_errno(-ret);
199:       ret = ERROR;
200:     }
201: 
202:   return ret;

40: /****************************************************************************
41:  * Name:  nxsched_add_readytorun
42:  *
43:  * Description:
44:  *   This function adds a TCB to the ready to run list.  If the currently
45:  *   active task has preemption disabled and the new TCB would cause this
46:  *   task to be pre-empted, the new task is added to the g_pendingtasks list
47:  *   instead.  The pending tasks will be made ready-to-run when preemption is
48:  *   unlocked.
49:  *
50:  * Input Parameters:
51:  *   btcb - Points to the blocked TCB that is ready-to-run
52:  *
53:  * Returned Value:
54:  *   true if the currently active task (the head of the ready-to-run list)
55:  *   has changed.
56:  *
57:  * Assumptions:
58:  * - The caller has established a critical section before calling this
59:  *   function (calling sched_lock() first is NOT a good idea -- use
60:  *   enter_critical_section()).
61:  * - The caller has already removed the input rtcb from whatever list it
62:  *   was in.
63:  * - The caller handles the condition that occurs if the head of the
64:  *   ready-to-run list is changed.
65:  *
66:  ****************************************************************************/
67: 
68: #ifndef CONFIG_SMP
69: bool nxsched_add_readytorun(FAR struct tcb_s *btcb)
70: {
71:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
72:   bool ret;
73: 
74:   /* Check if pre-emption is disabled for the current running task and if
75:    * the new ready-to-run task would cause the current running task to be
76:    * pre-empted.  NOTE that IRQs disabled implies that pre-emption is
77:    * also disabled.
78:    */
79: 
80:   if (rtcb->lockcount > 0 && rtcb->sched_priority < btcb->sched_priority)
81:     {
82:       /* Yes.  Preemption would occur!  Add the new ready-to-run task to the
83:        * g_pendingtasks task list for now.
84:        */
85: 
86:       nxsched_add_prioritized(btcb, list_pendingtasks());
87:       btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_PENDING;
88:       ret = false;
89:     }
90: 
91:   /* Otherwise, add the new task to the ready-to-run task list */
92: 
93:   else if (nxsched_add_prioritized(btcb, list_readytorun()))
94:     {
95:       /* The new btcb was added at the head of the ready-to-run list.  It
96:        * is now the new active task!
97:        */
98: 
99:       DEBUGASSERT(rtcb->lockcount == 0 && !is_idle_task(btcb));
100: 
101:       btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING;
102:       btcb->flink->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
103:       up_update_task(btcb);
104:       ret = true;
105:     }
106:   else
107:     {
108:       /* The new btcb was added in the middle of the ready-to-run list */
109: 
110:       btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
111:       ret = false;
112:     }
113: 
114:   return ret;
115: }
116: 
117: #else /* !CONFIG_SMP */
118: 
119: /****************************************************************************
120:  * Name:  nxsched_switch_running
121:  *
122:  * Description:
123:  *   This function switches the head of the current CPU's assigned tasks
124:  *   list to the TCB given as parameter. The idle task is not switched out.
125:  *   If the running task can't be swapped out, the btcb is pushed to
126:  *   the ready-to-run list.
127:  *
128:  * Input Parameters:
129:  *   cpu          - Always this_cpu(). Given as argument only for
130:  *                  optimization
131:  *   switch_equal - When true, switch away a task of equal priority compared
132:  *                  to the pending one
133:  *
134:  * Returned Value:
135:  *   true if the currently active task is switched
136:  *
137:  * Assumptions:
138:  * - The caller has established a critical section
139:  * - The caller has already removed the input rtcb from whatever list it
140:  *   was in.
141:  * - The caller handles the condition that occurs if the head of the
142:  *   assigned tasks list has changed.
143:  *
144:  ****************************************************************************/
145: 
146: bool nxsched_switch_running(int cpu, bool switch_equal)
147: {
148:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = current_task(cpu);
149:   int sched_priority = rtcb->sched_priority;
150:   FAR struct tcb_s *btcb;
151:   bool ret = false;
152: 
153:   DEBUGASSERT(cpu == this_cpu());
154: 
155:   if (nxsched_islocked_tcb(rtcb))
156:     {
157:       return false;
158:     }
159: 
160:   if (switch_equal && sched_priority > 0)
161:     {
162:       sched_priority--;
163:     }
164: 
165:   /* If there is a task in readytorun list, which is eglible to run on this
166:    * CPU, and has higher priority than the current task,
167:    * switch the current task to that one.
168:    */
169: 
170:   for (btcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
171:        btcb && btcb->sched_priority > sched_priority;
172:        btcb = btcb->flink)
173:     {
174:       /* Check if the task found in ready-to-run list is allowed to run on
175:        * this CPU. TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED may be used to override affinity. If
176:        * the flag is set, assume that btcb->cpu is valid, and it is the only
177:        * CPU on which the btcb can run.
178:        */
179: 
180:       if (CPU_ISSET(cpu, &btcb->affinity) &&
181:           ((btcb->flags & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED) == 0 || btcb->cpu == cpu))
182:         {
183:           /* Found a task, remove it from ready-to-run list */
184: 
185:           dq_rem((FAR struct dq_entry_s *)btcb, list_readytorun());
186: 
187:           if (!is_idle_task(rtcb))
188:             {
189:               /* Put currently running task back to ready-to-run list */
190: 
191:               rtcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
192:               nxsched_add_prioritized(rtcb, list_readytorun());
193:             }
194:           else
195:             {
196:               rtcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_ASSIGNED;
197:             }
198: 
199:           per_cpu_var_smp(g_assignedtasks, cpu) = btcb;
200:           up_update_task(btcb);
201: 
202:           btcb->cpu = cpu;
203:           btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING;
204:           ret = true;
205:           break;
206:         }
207:     }
208: 
209:   return ret;
210: }
211: 
212: /****************************************************************************
213:  * Name:  nxsched_add_readytorun
214:  *
215:  * Description:
216:  *   This function adds a TCB to one of the ready to run lists. The list
217:  *   will be:
218:  *
219:  *   1. The g_readytorun list if the task is ready-to-run but not running
220:  *      and not assigned to a CPU.
221:  *   2. The g_assignedtask[cpu] list if the task is running or if has been
222:  *      assigned to a CPU.
223:  *
224:  *   If the currently active task has preemption disabled and the new TCB
225:  *   would cause this task to be pre-empted, the new task is added to the
226:  *   g_pendingtasks list instead.  The pending tasks will be made
227:  *   ready-to-run when preemption isunlocked.
228:  *
229:  * Input Parameters:
230:  *   btcb - Points to the blocked TCB that is ready-to-run
231:  *
232:  * Returned Value:
233:  *   true if the currently active task (the head of the ready-to-run list)
234:  *   has changed.
235:  *
236:  * Assumptions:
237:  * - The caller has established a critical section before calling this
238:  *   function (calling sched_lock() first is NOT a good idea -- use
239:  *   enter_critical_section()).
240:  * - The caller has already removed the input rtcb from whatever list it
241:  *   was in.
242:  * - The caller handles the condition that occurs if the head of the
243:  *   ready-to-run list has changed.
244:  *
245:  ****************************************************************************/
246: 
247: bool nxsched_add_readytorun(FAR struct tcb_s *btcb)
248: {
249:   bool doswitch = false;
250:   int target_cpu = btcb->flags & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED ? btcb->cpu :
251:     nxsched_select_cpu(btcb->affinity);
252:   FAR struct tcb_s *tcb = current_task(target_cpu);
253: 
254:   /* Add the btcb to the ready to run list, and try to run it on the target
255:    * CPU
256:    */
257: 
258:   btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
259:   nxsched_add_prioritized(btcb, list_readytorun());
260: 
261:   /* In some cases, such as setaffinity, cpu need to be used. */
262: 
263:   btcb->cpu = target_cpu;
264:   if (tcb->sched_priority < btcb->sched_priority)
265:     {
266:       doswitch = nxsched_deliver_task(this_cpu(), target_cpu,
267:                                       SWITCH_HIGHER);
268:     }
269: 
270:   return doswitch;
271: }
272: 
273: #endif /* CONFIG_SMP */

44: static bool bk7258_hwspinlock_trylock(struct hwspinlock_dev_s *dev)
45: {
46:   unsigned int cpu = (unsigned int)up_cpu_index();
47:   unsigned int other = cpu ^ 1u;
48: 
49:   (void)dev;
50:   DEBUGASSERT(cpu < 2);
51:   bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_ENTRY);
52: 
53:   /* BK7258 has only two SRAM exclusive monitors while CP, AP CPU1 and AP
54:    * CPU2 are all active.  Keep the AP-only atomic gate independent of
55:    * LDAEX/STREX so CP traffic cannot starve an AP exclusive sequence.
56:    */
57: 
58:   /* libc atomics are normally short, but the scheduler's recursive critical
59:    * section can issue another atomic operation on the same CPU.  Re-entry
60:    * must be decided before entering Peterson arbitration; otherwise a waiter
61:    * on the other CPU can make the current owner wait for itself.
62:    */
63: 
64:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner == cpu + 1u)
65:     {
66:       if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth == UINT32_MAX)
67:         {
68:           PANIC();
69:         }
70: 
71:       g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth++;
72:       UP_DMB();
73:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_REENTER |
74:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.depth);
75:       return true;
76:     }
77: 
78:   /* This is only a fast rejection.  The Peterson protocol below remains
79:    * authoritative while a new owner is between intent and owner publish.
80:    */
81: 
82:   if (g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner != 0)
83:     {
84:       bk7258_hwspinlock_trace(cpu, BK7258_GATE_TRACE_OWNER_BUSY |
85:                              g_bk7258_atomic_gate.owner);
86:       return false;
87:     }
88: 
89:   /* Every attempt must publish a fresh intent and turn.  Leaving intent set
90:    * after a failed trylock makes the state stale and breaks trylock's
91:    * one-attempt contract.
92:    */

**Audit Result**

The SMP image in [`cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:420) was audited read-only. No files were modified. The separate [`out/beken_bk7258-ap_nsh`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/out/beken_bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:267) image is UP and does not match traces containing a secondary stage.

**Startup Trace**

1. `AppBringUp`, priority 100, calls `board_late_initialize()`. The board hook creates a detached priority-100 pthread with explicit CPU0 affinity and returns immediately: [`bk7258_bringup.c:201`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:201), [`bk7258_bringup.c:209`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:209), [`bk7258_bringup.c:221`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:221).

2. `AppBringUp` is therefore free to start priority-100 `nsh_main`; NSH does not wait for the detached board worker. The SMP default cpuset is both CPUs, while only the board worker is explicitly CPU0-only: [`.config:425`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:425), [`.config:431`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:431), [`.config:2600`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:2600).

3. `mailbox_workers_start()` waits for CPU1 scheduler readiness, pins its caller to CPU0, then creates `mbox-v2` at priority 105 and `mbox-diag` at 80: [`bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1091`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1091), [`bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1102`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1102), [`bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1118`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1118), [`bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1132`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1132).

4. `mb_uart_worker_start()` creates the CPU0-inheriting `mb-uart0` worker at priority 106: [`bk7258_mb_uart.c:551`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:551), [`bk7258_mb_uart.c:570`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:570).

5. SysTick starts on CPU0 and immediately becomes capable of preempting thread execution: [`bk7258_timerisr.c:61`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:61), [`bk7258_timerisr.c:69`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:69). Every tick updates `detail[3]` around `nxsched_process_timer()`: [`bk7258_timerisr.c:38`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:38).

6. Primary stage 31 is written immediately before `bk7258_mb_uart_start()`. Stage 45 is the next marker after that function returns, and stage 46 is written before `wait_link_ready()`: [`bk7258_bringup.c:90`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:90), [`bk7258_bringup.c:92`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:92), [`bk7258_bringup.c:94`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:94), [`bk7258_bringup.c:96`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:96), [`bk7258_bringup.c:98`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:98). SMP-image disassembly confirms this exact instruction order.

**Findings**

1. **High: stage-31 starvation is permitted by the priority topology.** The stage-owning thread is CPU0 priority 100; both transport workers are CPU0-only and higher priority, 105/106. Round-robin only shares time among equal priorities, so it cannot rescue priority 100 while either worker remains runnable. The source itself assumes they will “drain transport state and then block,” but does not enforce a work budget: [`bk7258_bringup.c:86`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:86).

2. **High: the UART worker can form a sustained callback/wakeup cycle.** It wakes or times out, clears the semaphore, performs one transport action, and then invokes the serial callback unconditionally, even on a no-progress timeout: [`bk7258_mb_uart.c:467`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:467), [`bk7258_mb_uart.c:493`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:493), [`bk7258_mb_uart.c:497`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:497). The callback can drain RX/TX upper-half loops: [`bk7258_serial.c:198`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_serial.c:198). Writes, RX, ACK completion, flow-control changes and state requests all repost the same worker semaphore, including self-reposts from callback-driven TX: [`bk7258_mb_uart.c:253`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:253), [`bk7258_mb_uart.c:372`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:372), [`bk7258_mb_uart.c:625`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:625), [`bk7258_mb_uart.c:671`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:671). Under continuous console traffic this can keep priority 106 runnable indefinitely.

3. **High: the AP SMP doorbell path has an unbounded FIFO-full spin.** `bk7258_smp_kick()` loops forever on `-EAGAIN`, with no limit, backoff, or deferred retry: [`bk7258_smpcall.c:78`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:78), [`bk7258_smpcall.c:99`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:99), [`bk7258_smpcall.c:117`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:117). UART RX can wake an NSH reader on CPU1, causing a cross-CPU scheduler delivery through this port. This is a real AP defect, although a CPU0 instance spinning inside a masked critical section would normally stop CPU0 SysTick; therefore continuous tick advancement argues that this loop is not continuously holding CPU0 during the sampled interval.

4. **High: worker creation success is mistaken for worker liveness.** Both transport workers can exit immediately on affinity or secondary-readiness failure, but startup stores only their PID/created flags and has no ready handshake or exit result: [`bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:966`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:966), [`bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:972`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:972), [`bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:977`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:977), [`bk7258_mb_uart.c:455`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:455). `g_workers_started=true` consequently proves creation, not that either worker remains alive.

5. **Medium: affinity setup is structurally correct but incompletely checked.** The bring-up pthread explicitly requests CPU0, the creator is pinned again before creating kernel workers, and NuttX child tasks inherit creator affinity. That is the correct topology. However all `pthread_attr_*` return values, including affinity, are ignored: [`bk7258_bringup.c:209`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:209). Worker self-binding failures are then silent except for thread exit.

6. **Medium: semaphore reset introduces real but bounded lost-wakeup windows.** Both workers call `nxsem_reset(..., 0)` immediately after waiting: [`bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:988`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:988), [`bk7258_mb_uart.c:467`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:467). A post between wait return and reset can be erased. Transport state, rings and pending flags remain authoritative, and both workers retry every 10 ms, so this should cause latency rather than permanent loss. The diagnostic worker can also coalesce and skip intermediate link callbacks: [`bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:925`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:925).

7. **Medium: `mb_uart_start()` does not wake the UART worker and cannot report failure.** It marks `state_pending`, starts transport recovery, ignores the probe return value, and returns `void`: [`bk7258_mb_uart.c:598`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:598). The initial UART action relies on the 10 ms timed worker pass or the later `wait_link_ready()` retry at [`bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1351`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1351).

8. **Medium: callbacks execute inside the global driver lock with interrupts masked.** TX completion and RX channel callbacks run under `g_bk7258_driver_lock`: [`bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:348`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:348), [`bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:793`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:793), [`bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:870`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:870). Current startup callbacks are bounded and do not sleep, but any future blocking or expensive callback would stop mailbox progress and increase cross-CPU lock latency.

9. **No fatal wait-loop defect found.** `wait_link_ready()` has an 8-second tick deadline, retries STATE every 100 ms, directly drains MBOX RX and sleeps 1 ms: [`bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1326`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1326). The physical IRQ drain is budgeted to eight FIFO entries: [`bk7258_mbox0.c:241`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mbox0.c:241), [`bk7258_mbox0.c:265`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mbox0.c:265). A genuine wait-loop stall would show stage 46, not 31.

**Why `primary=31`, Advancing Tick, And NSH Output Coexist**

Stage 31 proves timer start returned and the CPU0 tick was enabled, but only proves that the CPU0 priority-100 bring-up thread reached the call to `mb_uart_start()`. The higher-priority transport workers can take over at the link-state semaphore posts before stage 45 is written. SysTick still interrupts those workers and advances `detail[3]`. Meanwhile detached startup allowed priority-100 NSH to start independently and SMP can run it on CPU1. The priority-106 UART worker can establish the link and transport NSH output without the stage-owning thread resuming.

Consequently, persistent 31 with live tick and NSH is most consistent with CPU0 thread starvation or repeated preemption at/inside `mb_uart_start()`, not a stopped clock, failed secondary scheduler, or execution inside `wait_link_ready()`. If console traffic is finite, priority 100 should eventually resume; indefinite persistence requires a continuously runnable worker, an AP spin such as the IPI retry, or lock ownership that never clears.

**Safe AP-Only Options**

- Add boottrace substages inside `mb_uart_start()`: before driver-lock acquisition, after `state_pending`, before/after `start_probe()`, and before return. Add sampled worker phase counters around semaphore wait, driver lock, send, and serial callback.
- Record each worker’s entry CPU, affinity, priority, wait/wakeup counts, callback count, maximum callback duration, and terminal error in boottrace details or AP statistics.
- Add worker-ready semaphores/flags and verify them after SysTick starts but before stage 31. Clear an `alive` flag and record errno on every worker exit.
- Make `mb_uart_start()` return `int`, check `start_probe()`, and explicitly post `g_uart.worker_sem`.
- During this narrow startup window, run bring-up above 106 until it has written stage 46 and is about to block, then restore priority 100. Alternatively hold transport workers below bring-up until the wait begins.
- Invoke the serial callback only for an actual RX, TX-space, link, or flow-control event; remove unconditional callback execution after a pure 10 ms timeout. Add a bounded event budget so continuous CPU1 console production cannot monopolize CPU0.
- Replace the unbounded SMP FIFO loop with bounded attempts plus a guaranteed symmetric AP retry mechanism. Pending bits must remain set, but retry must exist for both CPU directions, preferably from mailbox-space/error IRQ handling or another per-core port hook. Reintroducing only a CPU0 SysTick retry would again lose CPU1-to-CPU0 doorbells.
- Keep `wait_link_ready()` and the NuttX scheduler unchanged. Its active RX drain, sleep and deadline are appropriate once stage 46 is reached.
